summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to run a Kea DHCPv4 server on the shared 10.100.56.0/24 network with static reservations for node2 and node3, and configured node2/node3 (RHEL7) to obtain their address from node1 rather than the platform's own DHCP responder. Since all three nodes share a single flat egress network where the platform gateway (10.100.56.1) also runs an active DHCP server, a `reject 10.100.56.1;` directive was added to dhclient config on node2/node3 so they deterministically source their lease from node1 instead of racing with the platform. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; boot IDs changed on each, and post-reboot state confirms node1's DHCP server auto-started and node2/node3 re-acquired their addresses (10.100.56.11/.12) via DHCPACK from node1 (10.100.56.10), preserving IPs and connectivity.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS 2026.04 rolling, node2/node3=RHEL7, all on single 10.100.56.0/24 network with platform DHCP server active at 10.100.56.1

Set node1 eth0 to static 10.100.56.10/24, added static default route via 10.100.56.1, configured Kea DHCPv4 (service dhcp-server) with subnet 10.100.56.0/24, pool 10.100.56.200-220, and static-mapping reservations for node2 (MAC 02:85:a4:4d:8a:13 -> .11) and node3 (MAC 02:0d:a8:ac:0e:b8 -> .12); committed and saved
Verified isc-kea-dhcp4-server active and generated Kea config matches intent

Discovered platform gateway (10.100.56.1) actively answers DHCP on the same broadcast domain; attempted iptables/firewalld blocking was ineffective since dhclient uses raw LPF sockets that bypass netfilter delivery
Removed the ineffective iptables/firewalld rules to keep the system clean
Added persistent `reject 10.100.56.1;` to /etc/dhcp/dhclient.conf and /etc/dhcp/dhclient-eth0.conf on node2 and node3 so dhclient ignores platform offers/acks and binds only to node1's Kea server
Validated via ifdown/ifup that node2 and node3 rebind their existing IPs (.11/.12) with DHCPOFFER/DHCPACK sourced from 10.100.56.10, and platform offers/naks are explicitly rejected
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy service/network baselines on all three nodes
Restarted node1 first (dependency for DHCP), confirmed boot_id changed, confirmed Kea DHCP server auto-started active and static IP/route/config persisted via 'save'
Restarted node2, confirmed boot_id changed, confirmed via NetworkManager journal that it acquired its lease from 10.100.56.10 (node1) at boot with unchanged IP 10.100.56.11
Restarted node3, confirmed boot_id changed, confirmed via NetworkManager journal that it acquired its lease from 10.100.56.10 (node1) at boot with unchanged IP 10.100.56.12
Cross-verified node1's Kea lease database (dhcp4-leases.csv) shows active current leases for node2 (10.100.56.11) and node3 (10.100.56.12) matching post-reboot timestamps

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart (DHCP config + static IP)
evidence.summary: node1 configured with static 10.100.56.10/24, Kea shared-network LAN with reservations for node2/node3, isc-kea-dhcp4-server active before restart

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 healthy baseline (obtaining DHCP address from node1, not platform)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed platform DHCP (10.100.56.1) winning; after adding reject directive on node2/node3, ifdown/ifup renewal confirmed DHCPACK from node1 (10.100.56.10) with rejection of platform offers/naks logged

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement + boot identity change
evidence.summary: reboot command dropped the exec stream (acknowledged before disconnect); polling timed out then boot_id changed from 7668189d-... to 88a04c3a-...

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery (DHCP server + config persistence)
evidence.summary: After reboot, isc-kea-dhcp4-server active, static IP 10.100.56.10/24 and default route via 10.100.56.1 intact, Kea pool config matches committed/saved config

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement + boot identity change
evidence.summary: reboot command closed connection (acknowledged); polling timed out/no-route then succeeded with boot_id changed from 9ed9e820-... to 3cfb33ab-...

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery: DHCP lease obtained from node1
evidence.summary: NetworkManager journal at boot shows DHCPACK from 10.100.56.1 explicitly rejected by rule, and DHCPOFFER/DHCPACK accepted from 10.100.56.10 (node1), binding to unchanged IP 10.100.56.11

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement + boot identity change
evidence.summary: reboot command closed connection (acknowledged); polling timed out then succeeded with boot_id changed from a8e7c48c-... to 1a6e1f4b-...

evidence.requirement: node3 post-restart recovery: DHCP lease obtained from node1
evidence.summary: NetworkManager journal at boot shows DHCPACK from 10.100.56.1 explicitly rejected by rule, and DHCPOFFER/DHCPACK accepted from 10.100.56.10 (node1), binding to unchanged IP 10.100.56.12

evidence.requirement: Cross-check: node1's DHCP server data confirms both clients as active leases post-recovery
evidence.summary: Kea lease database (dhcp4-leases.csv) on node1 shows current entries for node2 (10.100.56.11) and node3 (10.100.56.12) with hostnames and timestamps matching the post-reboot DHCP transactions
